note: Forest Service campground strung along a dead-end forest road in a hollow beside Paddy Creek, next to the Paddy Creek Wilderness; asphalt pads, some on the creek side and some under the bluff. Coming from the north, Paddy Creek Road fords the creek on a low-water slab just before the entrance: water runs over it at all times and it can be impassable after heavy rain. The approach from Highway 32 to the south does not cross it. Bring drinking water. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the Forest Service page: 19 FCFS sites, $15, no hookups, no water, to 34 ft, season Apr 1 - Dec 1. NEW: a closure order shuts the whole recreation area Dec 1 2026 - Dec 31 2027 (bank stabilization + bridge) - status written. Pin is on the day-use/low-water crossing, 350 m from the campground: move proposed. Creekside kept on the agency's wording.
flags: CLOSURE: Order 09-05-03-26-01 closes all of Paddy Creek Recreation Area and Forest Road 211 (the campground road) from Dec 1 2026 through Dec 31 2027 'while a contract is executed to restabilize the Paddy Creek campground bank and replace the Paddy Creek low water crossing with a bridge'. That is the entire 2027 season. status.temporarily_closed written with reopens 2028; the page banner still reads 'Site Open' for what is left of 2026 (to Dec 1). Stays in the database with the caveat.

PIN MOVE (350 m): stored 37.5559,-92.0426 is on Paddy Creek Road at the creek crossing / picnic area. The order's map puts the campground symbol at the far (south-east) end of FR 211, and the page gives 37.553462,-92.04029; on imagery that is the road's end loop under canopy. Proposed 37.55346,-92.04029.

LOW-WATER CROSSING: page directions from Roby and Fort Leonard Wood (north, via Slabtown Road): 'the recreation area is on the left, just over the low water crossing/bridge* - *Water flows over this crossing at all times, however it can be unpassable after a heavy rain.' From Licking (south, Highway 32, 8 miles of Paddy Creek Road): 'the rec area will be on the right just before the creek' - no crossing. No 4WD or clearance wording ('Vehicle Clearance - No restrictions'). Caveat written in the note; kept, as John Alva Fuson. The crossing is what the 2027 project replaces with a bridge.

WATERFRONT (stored creekside, kept, but NOT counted site by site): the sites are under closed canopy on leaf-off imagery, so no site could be named within 50 m on an open apron. What supports creekside is the agency: 'Paddy Creek Campground is nestled in a hollow along Paddy Creek', 'There is river and bluff side camping', and the closure order's purpose, 'to restabilize the Paddy Creek campground bank'. On imagery FR 211 runs 30-80 m from the creek for its whole length, the creek a 10-15 m stream in a wide gravel bed (creek class). Satellite does not veto; it does not confirm either. If the owner wants a counted basis this is a downgrade to not waterfront.
PHONE (none stored): the page lists the Houston/Rolla/Cedar Creek district office at 417-967-4194.
The 34-ft size line is this campground's own, and admits a 23-ft rig.
